question: Can a GENUINE multi-location home-service contractor (each location a real physical office with its own street address, staff, and Google Business Profile) scale a website into per-location silos — a base ~15-page site PLUS a full ~15-page silo per additional location, launching at ~10 locations (~150 pages total) — WITHOUT triggering Google's doorway-page, scaled-content-abuse, thin/templated-content, or unhelpful-content penalties, while achieving genuine per-page TOPIC-level uniqueness AND helpfulness? Prioritize PRIMARY current sources (Google Search Central docs/blog, web.dev) over SEO-blog opinion; label community/SEO sources as inference not policy. Latest-wins: 2024-2026 reality beats older lore.
subQuestions: What is Google's CURRENT (2024-2026) doorway-page and scaled-content-abuse policy (exact definition + enforcement), how did the March-2024 spam-policy consolidation and May-2024 scaled-content-abuse policy change it, and crucially how does Google distinguish a GENUINE multi-location business (real offices, each with its own address/staff/Google Business Profile) from FAKE single-office hyperlocal expansion (one office spinning up town pages for areas with no real presence)? When do legit franchises / multi-branch businesses rank without penalty vs get nuked?

What does the Helpful Content / people-first system (folded into core ranking March 2024) operationally require — what do 'helpfulness' and 'information gain' mean, what is the who/how/why self-assessment framework, and how does site-wide classifier drag from thin pages actually work?

Does Google weight percent word-level uniqueness or topic/intent-level uniqueness when judging templated location pages, and what is the real 2024-2026 threshold? Validate the 'Swap Test' (swap the city and the page should no longer read correctly) against current Google guidance and practitioner evidence.

Real 2024-2026 case studies: large multi-location / programmatic location-page sites that rank WITHOUT penalty, AND ones that got penalized/de-indexed — extract the concrete differentiators (real entity backing, information gain, genuine local value). Local home-service examples where possible.

What categories of genuinely-unique, helpful, per-location PUBLIC data exist for a home-service trade (roofing/HVAC/plumbing) — local climate/storm/hail history, permit data, building codes & local code requirements, housing-stock age/value, neighborhood & landmark names, HOA/permitting quirks, seasonal patterns, local hazards, demographic/market data — and WHERE to source each (specific APIs / public datasets)? Map each category to HOW it creates topic-level uniqueness (passes the Swap Test), not just local color.

Best practice for tying >=5 location-specific reviews/testimonials to each location (sprinkled through the silo and/or a dedicated per-location reviews page), Google's CURRENT stance on review/rating schema (is self-serving Review/AggregateRating markup on your own LocalBusiness penalized or ignored?), and how location-specific reviews drive uniqueness + E-E-A-T + local trust.

Recommended architecture for legit location silos: subfolder vs subdomain vs 'subsite'; internal-linking / siloing / link-graph design; schema (LocalBusiness / HomeAndConstructionBusiness per location, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList); canonical and areaServed handling. State a recommended per-location page set AND a safe site-wide page ceiling for a GENUINE multi-location business.
